actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 405 - 5 (Roll no. 9). (text: CR H100-101)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 405 - 5 (Roll no. 9). (text: CR H100-101)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H107-108)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 152.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H100-101)
Mr. Graves moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill.
Referred to the Subcommittee on Economic Development, Public Buildings, and Emergency Management.
Referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

dimensions.assessment: Affects disaster assistance applicants, grantees, FEMA, the Small Business Administration, HUD, and other federal agencies participating in the working group.
dimensions.evidence: collection of information from disaster assistance applicants and grantees will be made less burdensome, duplicative, and time consuming for applicants and grantees

dimensions.assessment: Aims to reduce administrative burdens and duplication in disaster relief applications and damage assessments rather than altering relief benefit levels directly.
dimensions.evidence: identify and describe the potential areas of duplication or fragmentation in preliminary damage assessments after disaster declarations

dimensions.assessment: Requires administrative studies and reporting without authorizing new funding or altering federal disaster spending totals.
Modifies a previous statutory provision (Disaster Recovery Reform Act of 2018) to mandate interagency coordination, reporting plans, and public website creation.
dimensions.evidence: Section 1223 of the Disaster Recovery Reform Act of 2018 (Public Law 115-254) is amended to read as follows

dimensions.assessment: Sets two-year deadlines for studies, plans, and reports, with ongoing public reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this section, the Administrator... shall-- (1) conduct a study and develop a plan

missing_information: Estimates of administrative cost savings resulting from streamlined information collection.
importance_detail.rationale: This bill directs FEMA to conduct studies, develop streamlining plans for disaster assistance information collection, convene an interagency working group on preliminary damage assessments, and report to Congress.

card.summary: The FEMA Act of 2025 reestablishes the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) as an independent, cabinet-level agency separate from the Department of Homeland Security. It enacts extensive reforms to FEMA's public assistance, individual assistance, and hazard mitigation programs, aiming to speed up disaster funding, reduce paperwork, and improve transparency.
